hints.content: In order to find $F'(1)$, we should first find an expression for $F'(x)$ (for any input $x$) in terms of $g$, $h$, and their derivatives.

So $F'(x)=\dfrac{g'(x)h(x)-g(x)h'(x)}{[h(x)]^2}$.

We can now plug $x=1$ into this expression:

$F'(1)=\dfrac{g'(1)h(1)-g(1)h'(1)}{[h(1)]^2}$

We are given that $g(1)=5$ and $g'(1)=-3$.

Since $h(x)=x^2$, we know that $h(1)=1$ and $h'(1)=2$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

Let's plug in those values!

$\begin{align}
F'(1)&=\dfrac{(-3)(1)-(5)\left(2\right)}{(1)^2}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{-13}{1}
\\\\
&=-13
\end{align}$

### Finding $h(1)$

$\begin{align}
h(\blueD{1})&=(\blueD1)^2
\\\\
&=1
\end{align}$

### Finding $h'(x)$

$\begin{align}
h'(x)&=\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^2\right)
\\\\
&=2x
\end{align}$

### Finding $h'(1)$

$\begin{align}
h'(\blueD{1})&=2(\blueD 1)
\\\\
&=2
\end{align}$
